html:
The Amahuaca are a Panoan people of the southwestern Amazon, on the upper Ucayali and Juruá headwaters in Peru, with a few in Acre, Brazil.

They lived in small scattered groups, farming maize and manioc and hunting, and were largely isolated until the 1700s and 1800s. The rubber boom brought raids and forced labour, and in recent decades loggers, oil prospectors and disease have pressed on their land. In 1998 they numbered only about 520. Related Panoan neighbours include the Yaminawá, the Shipibo-Konibo and the Huni Kuin. The Arawakan Yine live nearby.
sum: The Amahuaca are a Panoan people of the southwestern Amazon, on the upper Ucayali and Juruá headwaters in Peru, with a few in Acre, Brazil.
